B names engineering difficulty as its main risk and offers no fix for it; its points on bulk-accept and change size are only design details, not a stated risk. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers firmly choose inline tracked changes and tie it to the traceability requirement. Both also explain well why copy-paste hides changes and breaks the link to a person's decision, and both keep the chat panel only as a way to propose tracked suggestions. B is stronger on risks of the chosen design: it names redline fatigue and rubber-stamping and gives a fix for each. A's main stated risk is engineering effort, and it raises 'no accept all' only as a design detail.
